question.text: If EURUSD spot is 1.0800, US 6-month rate is 5.0% p.a. and Eurozone 6-month rate is 3.5% p.a., what is the 6-month EURUSD forward price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (p.63), F = S x (1 + RQC x Period) / (1 + RBC x Period), where RQC is the quote currency's rate and RBC is the base currency's rate. For EURUSD, EUR is the base (RBC = 3.5%) and USD is the quote (RQC = 5%). F = 1.0800 x (1 + 0.05 x 0.5) / (1 + 0.035 x 0.5) = 1.0800 x 1.025 / 1.0175 = ~1.0880. The Trap: 1.0722 results from swapping the rates and using the EUR rate as RQC; RQC must always be the interest rate of the quote currency. Note: Page 64 records the high-rate currency discount principle: the currency with the higher interest rate trades at a forward discount, so with USD rates above EUR rates, USD weakens forward, which is why EURUSD forward > spot.
